Agree with the approach. A few concrete recommendations from finance/ops perspective:

1) Concession amount: We can approve a price concession in the 8-12% band under commercial delegated authority, but anything above 10% will require FP&A/Revenue Ops approval. The $75k platform credit is OK if structured as a one-time pre-paid credit (applied to invoice schedule) — helpful to lock usage.

2) SLO structure: Offer 99.9% monthly throughput availability for the committed baseline. If SLO missed, provide a credit equal to 5% of monthly committed spend per breach (caps at one monthly credit per month). This protects both sides and buys us margin predictability.

3) Pool sizing & burst: Recommend we size the pool for baseline steady-state at 40 vGPU-equivalents (based on their numbers) with a burst buffer that can autoscale to 65 for short windows. Pricing tiers should reflect baseline vs burst hours; commit covers baseline hours only.

4) Commercial trade-offs: If Aequitas can extend commit to 30 months or increase committed spend by 15%, we can push to 12% concession and the same $75k credit.

If we need an exec exception memo for >10% or for non-standard terms, I can draft.

Marcus
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
